input: Look into freelance writing gigs online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Freelance writing covers a huge range — blog posts, copywriting, technical writing, journalism, ghostwriting, etc. Knowing the niche determines where to look and how to position.

Whether this is a complete beginner or someone with existing clips/experience changes the entire strategy — beginners need portfolio-building steps, experienced writers need pitch and rate optimization.
If this needs to replace a full-time income vs. earn side money, the urgency, volume of outreach, and acceptable rates all shift dramatically.
There are many platforms (Upwork, Fiverr, ProBlogger, direct pitching, etc.) — knowing if the user has a preferred platform or wants to compare options shapes the immediate next steps.
The target client type (small businesses, agencies, publications, startups) affects where to search, how to pitch, and what rates are realistic.
Some writers want long-term retainer clients; others prefer one-off projects. This affects which platforms and outreach strategies to prioritize.
Success could mean landing a first gig within a week, hitting a monthly income target, or simply having a shortlist of platforms to apply to — this defines when the task is truly done.

gold.taskTitle: Find and Pursue Freelance Writing Gigs Online
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore and potentially land freelance writing opportunities available online.

questions.title: What type of writing do you want to focus on?
questions.description: E.g., blog content, copywriting, technical writing, creative writing, journalism, ghostwriting.

questions.title: How much freelance writing experience do you currently have?
questions.description: E.g., complete beginner with no clips, some personal projects, or prior paid experience.

questions.title: Is this meant to be a side income or replace full-time income?
questions.description: Determines the urgency, target earnings, and how aggressively to pursue gigs.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred platform in mind to start with?
questions.description: E.g., Upwork, Fiverr, ProBlogger job board, LinkedIn, or cold pitching directly.

questions.title: What kind of clients do you most want to write for?
questions.description: E.g., small businesses, marketing agencies, tech startups, online publications, or individual bloggers.

questions.title: Do you prefer ongoing retainer work or one-off project gigs?
questions.description: This shapes which platforms and outreach strategies are most worth pursuing.

questions.title: What does success look like at the end of this task?
questions.description: E.g., a shortlist of platforms to apply to, one paying client secured, or a specific monthly income target reached.
